title: Sales Enablement: Positioning & Messaging, Competitive Briefs, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies, Security FAQ (Prospects)
author: Jordan Patel
body:
Overview

This document is the canonical sales enablement playbook for Redwood Inference covering: positioning and messaging, short competitive briefs, recommended pitch deck flow, pricing guidance for common prospect scenarios, two representative customer case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this playbook when preparing calls, proposals, and RFP responses.

Owners and contacts
- Primary owner: Jordan Patel (Go-to-Market)
- Technical SME: Ethan Li (Solutions Engineering)
- Security SME: Priya Kaur (Security & Compliance)
- Product liaison: Maria Gomez (Product Marketing)

Audience and use cases
- AE / SDR call prep: quick positioning and 2–3 competitive rebuttals
- Solutions engineering: technical deep-dive and PoC checklist
- Customer success: onboarding expectations and SLA guidance
- Marketing: slide content and case study factsheets

1) Positioning & messaging pillars
- Core one-liner: "Redwood Inference makes high-performance, reliable LLM inference predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
- Value pillars (use these as the top-level bullets in discovery and pitch decks):
  - Production-first performance: predictable latency and throughput with GPU-optimized serving runtime and smart routing.
  - Deployment flexibility: hosted API for speed, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictability, Private (VPC/on‑prem) for regulated workloads.
  - Cost control levers: intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles reduce per-token unit cost.
  - Observability & guardrails: token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and quality/regression monitoring.
  - Reliability & fallbacks: automated regional/variant routing and graceful degradation policies.

Messaging dos and don'ts
- Do: lead with SLOs and predictable economics for production apps (e.g., p95 latency, committed throughput).
- Do: cite concrete levers (batching, caching, quantization) when asked about cost.
- Don't: claim to be a managed model training platform—focus on inference and serving.
- Don't: overcommit on model-specific accuracy; tie quality to evals and regression monitoring.

2) Quick competitive brief (one-paragraph + 3-point comparison)
- Competitor: Generic Cloud AI Endpoint providers (CLOUD-A)
  - Short: CLOUD-A emphasizes seamless model access and large model catalog, but often lacks cost controls and private deployment options at scale.
  - Comparison (Redwood vs CLOUD-A):
    - Deployment options: Redwood = Hosted / Dedicated / Private; CLOUD-A = Hosted / managed endpoints (limited private topology).
    - Cost controls: Redwood = batching, caching, quantization recommendations; CLOUD-A = primarily instance-based pricing.
    - Observability: Redwood = token-level, per-route dashboards + eval regressions; CLOUD-A = metrics + logs, less model-quality telemetry.

- Competitor: Open-Source Inference Stack (SELF-HOSTED)
  - Short: SELF-HOSTED offers full control and low per-instance cost but requires heavy infra investment and lacks integrated routing, billing, and enterprise SLAs.
  - Comparison:
    - Time-to-value: Redwood = hours to production (hosted + templates); SELF-HOSTED = weeks/months for infra + ops.
    - Operational risk: Redwood = SLA, automatic fallbacks; SELF-HOSTED = team-run capacity and incident load.
    - Feature completeness: Redwood = built-in quality monitoring, rollouts, and console; SELF-HOSTED = custom tooling required.

- Competitor: LLM API-first providers (API-X)
  - Short: API-X focuses on simplicity and model features; Redwood emphasizes predictable economics, private deployments, and enterprise-grade observability.
  - Comparison:
    - Enterprise readiness: Redwood = Dedicated + Private + compliance features; API-X = limited enterprise controls.
    - Cost predictability: Redwood = reserved capacity and cost-optimization toolkit; API-X = usage-only with less tooling to reduce unit costs.
    - Support & SLAs: Redwood = contracts and SRE-backed SLAs for Dedicated; API-X = limited commercial SLAs.

3) Pitch deck recommended flow (10–12 slides, summary bullets for each)
1. Title / customer logo + one-liner (use the core one-liner).
2. The opportunity (why inference costs, latency, and reliability matter for the buyer).
3. Redwood value proposition (three pillars: performance, flexibility, cost controls).
4. How it works (serving runtime, smart routing, caching, deployment modes) — include simple diagram.
5. Deployment options & timeline (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) — include typical lead times and pre-reqs.
6. Performance benchmarks (p50/p95 latency, throughput examples) — use customer anonymized benchmarks where possible.
7. Cost optimization levers (batching, caching, quantization) with expected % improvements.
8. Reliability & SLOs (SLA options, fallbacks, incident playbook).
9. Security & compliance (KMS/HSM, VPC, audit logs) — refer to Security FAQ.
10. Case study (one customer success slide with metrics).
11. Commercials (pricing model, Dedicated commit options, next steps).
12. Appendix / FAQs (sizing guidance, integration checklist).

Speaker notes (key talking points)
- Emphasize production economics: how batching/caching reduce per-token costs without sacrificing latency for typical web-app workloads.
- For regulated customers, lead with Private deployment and audit log features.
- When asked about migration: recommend a staged plan (pilot on Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private if needed).

4) Pricing guidance (high-level rules of thumb and example scenarios)
- Pricing model primitives:
  - Hosted API: pay-as-you-go (per-token generation + embeddings).
  - Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity with monthly/annual commits and overage rates.
  - Private: platform fee + optional support and deployment services.
- Commercial levers to offer in negotiation:
  - Short pilot credits for Hosted API (30–90 days) to validate integration.
  - Early-commit discounts for Dedicated (3/6/12 month tiers).
  - Volume tiering on generation tokens and embeddings.
  - Professional services add-on for Private deployments (integration, hardening).

Example pricing scenarios (illustrative)
- SMB chatbot pilot (10k monthly active users, 50k generations/day): Hosted + pilot credits; estimate: $X/month (provide actual numbers in the quote tool).
- Mid-market product personalization (real-time inference, p95 < 150ms): Dedicated small pool (1–2 nodes) with reserved throughput; recommend 6–12 month commit.
- Regulated enterprise (PHI/PII): Private deployment + support + compliance add-on; include security scoping and professional services.

Discounting guidance and approval matrix
- Up to 20% list discount: AE approval with standard deal justification.
- 20–40%: Sales manager + RevOps approval and defined commit.
- >40%: VP Sales + Finance and executive review.

5) Case studies (two representative vignettes for slides / one-pagers)
- Case study A: eCom personalization (Customer: anonymized RetailCo)
  - Problem: inconsistent personalization latency and high token costs at peak traffic.
  - Solution: migrated edge generation to Redwood Dedicated with prefix caching and model quantization.
  - Results: 45% reduction in per-unit inference cost, p95 latency improved from 320ms to 120ms, and capacity-related errors dropped to <0.1% over 30 days.
  - Who to quote: Solutions Engineering (contact Ethan Li) for architecture diagram.

- Case study B: Regulated financial assistant (Customer: anonymized FinServ)
  - Problem: strict data residency and audit requirements, plus need for deterministic SLAs.
  - Solution: Private deployment in customer VPC with customer KMS integration and daily audit exports.
  - Results: Achieved SOC-like evidence for auditors, SLA met for 99.95% uptime during pilot, and onboarding completed in 8 weeks including compliance validation.

6) Prospect Security FAQ (short-form answers for pitch/SDR use)
Q: Where does customer data reside when using Hosted API?
A: Customer data is processed in the region selected for the account and deleted per retention settings; logs can be restricted and streaming payloads can be excluded from persistent storage. For regulated customers we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments.

Q: Do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
A: Yes. Redwood supports customer-managed encryption keys for Private and Dedicated deployments; Hosted customers can opt into KMS integration in select tiers.

Q: Is Redwood SOC2 / ISO compliant?
A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II readiness and has completed third-party audits for our core hosted control plane. For detailed evidence, engage security@redwood-inference.com to begin the compliance review.

Q: How are access controls and RBAC implemented?
A: Role-based access control is available in Console with granular roles for admin, developer, and auditor. Private deployments integrate with customer SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning.

Q: How do you handle PII/PHI?
A: We recommend Private deployments for PHI. For Hosted/Dedicated, we provide data isolation options, encrypted-at-rest storage, and a documented data handling policy. We work with customers to implement data minimization and redaction when necessary.

Q: What logging and audit capabilities exist?
A: Audit logs include admin actions, model deployment events, and route-level usage. Daily export and long-term retention add-ons are available for compliance customers.

7) Sales play / call checklist (pre-call and post-call items)
Pre-call (AE / SE):
- Confirm prospect use case and SLO requirements (latency, throughput, residency).
- Prepare one tailored bench-mark (p95 latency / throughput) and a case study that maps closest to the prospect.
- Validate which deployment mode prospect prefers (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).

During call:
- Use the value pillars to align with prospect pain.
- Surface 2–3 concrete levers to reduce cost.
- Ask about compliance requirements early if enterprise.

Post-call (follow-up):
- SE: send tailored technical appendix and integration checklist within 24 hours.
- AE: prepare rough commercial framework and next-step recommendation (pilot / POC / scoping).
